note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 at HEAD 635aa08b78 (independent judge, clean clone), after b80a2eda36, 000e6fdfea and dc7de8e76f. RFC 3948 Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." THE TWO EARLIER FINDINGS ARE FIXED. Rekey: TestRFC3948RekeyedChildKeepsInnerAddress (both Child SA rekey directions, old pair retired, peer b refused TS_UNACCEPTABLE with nothing installed) goes red when newRekeyedChild drops innerGuard (re-probed). Production wiring: TestRFC3948ResponderSessionsShareInnerRegistry, TestRFC3948ResponderSAInitRefusesHeldInnerAddress, TestRFC3948ZeIKERekeyKeepsInnerRegistry, TestRFC3948PeerIKERekeyKeepsInnerRegistry and TestRFC3948InitiatorSessionRefusesHeldInnerAddress drive sessions built by startPeerSession over one SATable; re-probed in the clone (go -overlay, tree untouched): register.go's sa.innerSelectors assignment nil -> four wiring units red; both rekey.go innerSelectors inheritances nil -> three red; newChildSA's registry nil, installChildSA's claim removed, claim skipping every mode, innerSelectorPairsOf recording no pair, PolicySelectorsOverlap never true -> 13 to 14 tagged units red each; createFirstChildSA's no-dataplane claim removed -> TestRFC3948InitiatorSessionRefusesHeldInnerAddress and TestRFC3948ResponderSessionsShareInnerRegistry red (the wiring units run with no dataplane); strand turned into release, or settleStranded always releasing -> TestRFC3948FailedPolicyRemovalKeepsRecord and TestRFC3948StrandedRecordRefusesOverlap red. With the narrowing filter disabled the tagged set stays green, correctly: the install backstop still refuses. RETRY LOCK: removing retryMu from claim, or from retryStranded, leaves every tagged unit green; only the untagged TestStrandedRetryHoldsClaim and TestStrandedRetryDoesNotRemoveFreshPolicy go red. That is not a 5.1 hole: without the lock a retry deletes the policy a fresh Child SA just installed (same peer on XFRM, any peer on VPP), so a tunnel loses its policy, but the registry still holds that Child SA and every overlapping peer is still refused; no second SA leads to the address. WHY STILL WEAK, finding 1 (code, the requirement is not met on one path): a tunnel Child SA is never compared with another peer's TRANSPORT-mode Child SA. innerSelectorGuard.claim returns nil for modeTransport, so transport pairs are never held, and dataplane policyOwners.claim compares overlap only transport against transport (holder.transport), and tunnel against nothing but an identical key. Probe (scratch test, both orders): transport peer b at 198.18.0.9 (TSi 198.18.0.9/32, TSr 192.0.2.1/32) and unbound tunnel peer a proposing TSi 198.18.0.9/32, TSr 0.0.0.0/0 are BOTH served; their out policies 0.0.0.0/0->198.18.0.9/32 (tunnel) and 192.0.2.1/32->198.18.0.9/32 (transport) overlap at the same priority 2000, as do the in policies. Scenario: b is a host-to-host transport peer (BGP or GRE protected to 198.18.0.9); a, any authenticated peer bound to no pool, proposes 198.18.0.9/32 as its inner address; SGW now holds two SAs that lead to 198.18.0.9, unordered, so the gateway's own traffic to b goes into whichever policy the kernel met first, and in tunnel-first order b's traffic goes to a. Fix: hold transport Child SA pairs in innerSelectorRegistry too (marked transport), refuse a tunnel pair that overlaps another owner's transport pair and a transport pair that overlaps another owner's tunnel pair (transport against transport stays with policyOwners under Section 5.2), and add a negative unit tagged RFC3948-5.1-1 covering both arrival orders with a discrimination record. Finding 2 (test): the operator-fixed half of operatorOrdered is proven by no test. Making the p or the h operatorFixed check pass always, or dropping sameInnerSelector's protocol or port comparison, leaves the whole scoped set green (tagged and untagged), because every overlap case runs at equal priority, where the priority clause refuses on its own. The discrimination record of TestRFC3948ConfiguredOverlapNarrowedByPeerRefused (break: sameInnerSelector returning true) NO LONGER REDDENS the unit: replayed in the clone, it passes. ./le rfc check still accepts it because the record's fingerprints are sameInnerSelector and the unit, and the change that made the break harmless was the priority clause added to operatorOrdered, another function. The unit's claim, refused 'because a narrowed remote half is the peer's choice and not an operator-fixed selector', is wider than what it now checks. Scenario: b configured with remote 10.1.2.0/24 at policy-priority 1000 and negotiating it whole, unbound a at 2000 proposing 10.1.2.3/32; with the classification wrong, a is admitted and two SAs lead to 10.1.2.3. Fix: run the narrowed-by-peer case and a peer-chosen-against-fixed case at distinct priorities so only the operator-fixed classification refuses them, and re-record their breaks. Minor, not counted: installChildTolerant's no-dataplane claim can be removed with no test red anywhere; with no dataplane nothing is installed, so no packet can meet two SAs. Support remaining in rfc/short/rfc3948.md says Section 5.1 is met for every tunnel-mode peer; finding 1 makes that false for a tunnel peer overlapping a transport peer.
